description: Canonical reverse-coverage registry for testable normative clauses. Each row pins one protocol obligation to a stable clause_id, an exact prose anchor, a digest of that section's current text, and the evidence that proves it. It closes the direction vector-registry.json cannot: from prose obligation to executable proof. See spec/v1/zh/conformance/conformance-suite.md section 2.

coverage_scope.rule: This registry covers the high-risk observable obligation set named in included_categories. It is deliberately not a numbering of every normative sentence under spec/v1/zh; mechanically numbering prose would manufacture meaningless MUSTs. A green release gate proves that every registered clause has live evidence and that no registered section changed without review. It does NOT prove that every MUST in the specification is registered.
coverage_scope.extension_rule: Adding or changing a high-risk observable obligation that this registry is intended to evidence requires adding or updating a clause in the same change. Obligations without executable evidence stay explicitly outside this registry rather than pointing at unrelated evidence. Because section_digest pins registered anchors, editing a registered section fails the release gate until its existing clause and evidence are re-reviewed; this rule does not imply exhaustive coverage of every normative sentence in an included category.

registry_rules: clause_id values are stable and MUST NOT be reused after a clause is retired; retire a clause by setting status=deprecated instead of deleting the row.
source_anchor MUST be a repository-relative markdown path plus an existing heading slug. section_digest MUST equal the sha256 of that heading's section text as computed by tools/artifact_lint.

testability_grade=vector rows MUST list evidence_refs containing active vector ids from vector-registry.json. testability_grade=api_shape or audit rows MUST instead declare test_plan describing the non-vector proof.
A clause MUST NOT claim evidence it does not have: an obligation with no executable proof stays out of this registry rather than pointing at an unrelated vector.

clauses.requirement: Canonical JSON serialization (key order, number form, NFC strings, duplicate-key rejection) is the single encoding used for every digest, signature and canonical comparison.
Digest suite identifiers, canonical event digest computation and the bytewise tie-break order are fixed; implementations MUST NOT substitute another hash encoding or comparison direction.

The signature carrier MUST cryptographically protect its algorithm selection, and the binding payload MUST bind domain and audience; a signature valid for one algorithm, domain or audience MUST NOT verify for another. Section 6.0.2 fixes one construction for every registered proof context: the unsigned projection deletes the proof carrier member rather than nulling it and never defaults an absent optional, an absent optional binding field is omitted rather than written as null, audience is a single string or a duplicate-free array with the single-value form mandatory for one audience, and the context constant is a binding object member rather than a JWS header parameter, so a signature valid under one object family's context MUST NOT verify for another.

HLC well-formedness, logical-counter overflow handling and the causal-first usage boundary: HLC breaks ties between causally incomparable items only and MUST NOT select a winner in shared protocol state.
Cursors are opaque server-issued tokens bound to their query scope; clients MUST NOT parse or forge them and cross-scope replay MUST be rejected.
Encrypted envelopes carry a pre-encryption immutable header; AAD digest and ciphertext digest are computed over fixed transcripts and any mismatch MUST fail closed.
Transport encoding bounds: Content-Encoding is forbidden on non-streaming JSON operations and every size limit MUST be enforced before the body is fully buffered or parsed.
Every operation_id ends with <kind>.<action> drawn from the closed kind set, and the action MUST describe a protocol effect rather than an HTTP method name.
clauses.test_plan: Enforced mechanically by tools/artifact_lint: every operation_id in operation-registry.json is checked against the closed kind set and against forbidden HTTP-method action names. There is no runtime vector because the obligation is on the published contract, not on request handling.

clauses.requirement: Every write operation declares a machine-readable idempotency mechanism and retry safety; clients MUST NOT be left to guess the recovery path of an uncertain outcome.
Protected current-v1 endpoints require sender-constrained proof of possession; a bare bearer session grant MUST NOT authenticate a protected request.

MLS integration boundary: only registered active ciphersuites reach the wire; Welcome and KeyPackage binding is verified byte-exactly; every peer claim binds the accepted authorization Event id, its independently verifiable unique producer proof and signer evidence, and a destination-signed claim receipt without separate PCR/device/Agent history sidecars; encryption floors MUST NOT be downgraded; every encrypted envelope uses only the minimal encryption_context wire and reconstructs the exact closed pre-encryption header from the outer signed Event, verified producer domain, scope-derived group id and exact winning group state; MLS leaf ownership and Proposal targets preserve complete ActorId including Station and never collapse to the signing principal, and a minimal-metadata Realm-local pairwise actor is no exception: its Realm state stays keyed by the complete ActorId, and only the two closed out-of-Realm matching sites (consent peer, KeyPackage claim) use (realm_id, principal_id), which its did:key principal already pins; every MLS epoch binds the security frontier for its accepted key-access state, while a governance-result consumer may verify an authenticated scope-authorized single-authority conclusion under the same explicit governance trust boundary without replaying unrelated private control history; and epoch-0 leaf indices are recovered only from digest-verified RFC 9420 GroupInfo/ratchet-tree bytes committed by the accepted genesis. Realm/Circle Proposal/Commit wire inputs are complete PublicMessage MLSMessages; the governance Station check public signatures/tree transitions and persist exact consumed-proposal leaf provenance without member MAC secrets. Remove+Add always creates new provenance even when the leaf tuple is unchanged; minimal identities remain pairwise and Sidecar keeps its separate contract. Ordinary clients obtain exact historical Agent signing keys from their own Station instead of replaying public governance; they still verify the actual producer signature and historical MLS binding. Current self signing-key results serve only their requesting validation/in-flight identical query and cannot be reused for future Signals or operations. Message prepare distinguishes local plaintext intent from the encrypted wire request: the client freezes AAD inputs and encrypts locally, checks returned ciphertext/metadata and bindings byte-for-byte, and exact retry never consumes another sender counter. Plaintext is rejected under e2ee_required; the two-request path assumes send readiness and local MLS state.
Directory resolution failures are indistinguishable: unauthorized, non-existent and policy-denied targets MUST NOT be separable by error code, field set or timing.

Execution is derived from all effective registered writes. Any security write makes the whole Event atomic and confirmation-dependent. Closed bootstrap units activate only as complete registered units; ordinary subsequent data requires no new Seal.

Seal identity hashes its exact unsigned body; the sole commit transcript is {context,seal_digest}. Configuration, position, predecessor and results are transitively bound through that digest. Security state roots retain exact revisions including written null. The governance Station validates complete execution; consumers verify the configured signature and exact authorized facts. No Byzantine fault tolerance or automatic leader election is promised.

A grant stays within the union of the authorities its issuer_authority_refs name and within their per-action validity window. A grant without ordinary authority_control cannot be a grant ref; a ref with authority_regrant_allowed=false can issue only an explicitly terminal max_authority_depth=0 child. A grant ref supplies issuer authority only when its concrete subject ActorId equals the child issuer ActorId in full; cycles, inactive refs and same-DID cross-Station replay MUST fail closed rather than widen the effective permission set.
Revocation rolls back downstream grants and forces a re-check of dependent decisions; a revoked grant MUST NOT keep authorizing pending or cached writes.

Ordinary causal_register preserves coverage and every active Event identity, including equal values and explicit null. Join is idempotent, commutative and associative only within the same eligibility context. Apply authorization closure before causal coverage, retain values needed for reclassification, and merge raw evidence before recomputing across contexts. Security sequenced_state has no unordered join; transition tables and CAS remain validation predicates.

Field patches apply atomically against the declared pre-state; a partially applied patch or an unbound pre-state MUST be rejected. $op="unset" MUST NOT remove a registered redactable content-carrier slot, while $op="set" on the same slot and $op="unset" on metadata paths MUST be accepted. A patch path MUST NOT address a reducer-managed field of the target object kind; the per-object forbidden set, its universal minimum set and its one named View state exemption are read from registry/reducer-managed-path-registry.json, never re-derived from prose.
Every reducer-input event kind declares a closed cell contract (cell family, subject, lattice, bottom, effect projection); an unregistered projection MUST NOT be improvised.

Call state transitions follow the registered matrix, terminal states are absorbing, exact Event replay is a no-op, and competing commands against one revision produce one confirmed successor plus durable stale rejection outcomes. Compact media bindings carry only expires_at/issuer_kid/sig; rebuild the signed seven-tuple from the exact enclosing Event/Call and roster entry, require its frozen focus to match the accepted selection on write, and never reinterpret old signatures using a later focus.

Invite claim is a state machine: a consumed token MUST NOT be re-subjected, expiry uses canonical time, and the claimed lifecycle transition is atomic with its subject-bound membership proposal; only invite acceptance writes member state. Directed invite live uniqueness is carried by the registered ak.component.invite.live_target.v1 slot: create claims it under a head_eq null precondition, an unwritten cell reading null rather than a sentinel, every transition leaving the live set releases it under a head_eq create_event_id precondition, send_failed keeps it claimed, and a duplicate create is rejected with failed_precondition and invite_live_target_occupied at zero writes.

Account Data keys are server-versioned compare-and-set registers with explicitly registered writer authority and holder self operations: a stale write MUST fail with cas_conflict, the revision high-water mark never goes backwards, and domain merge runs client-side on plaintext.
Multi-device read cursor merge is causal-first: a causally dominating position wins regardless of HLC, HLC decides only concurrent positions, and device_id only breaks equal HLCs.
To-device delivery executes each durable handler effect exactly once: redelivery is deduplicated by the closed sender endpoint plus device_message_id and queue removal happens only on explicit ack.

Any eligible receiving Station independently verifies the original producer and portable authority evidence. Ordinary publication requires neither origin countersignature nor a new Seal nor a cache freshness lease. Known revocation serializes with the local live gate; unknown revocation has a propagation window. Historical eligibility is recomputed from exact closures, while confirmed security outcomes retain their frozen dependencies.

Every accountable principal on an Actor Event must have an active matching accountability grant; any missing grant rejects the whole Event without a stripped projection. One accountability record has two registered sources -- the standalone grant and the atomic projection an agent provision writes in its controller PCR -- and a verifier must accept both rather than searching only the general kind. Both key the cell by issuer principal, subject principal and the normalized scope set, and both project the same closed value of issuer, subject, normalized scope, not_before, optional expires_at and grant_status; a provision derives not_before from the envelope creation time it also has to match in its payload, omits expires_at rather than writing null, and is active. Neither source may put its event reference or inner proof into the value, because two endorsements that mean the same thing would then differ only by origin and collide on a reject cell.

Realm proposal configuration must leave a realizable decision schedule: decision window does not exceed the absolute deadline, equality is valid only when deferral is disabled, and invalid create/update writes reject without state change.
Optional nullable fields normalize absent and null unless a conditional branch requires the field or x-arkret-presence-semantics=distinct explicitly assigns three business states.
clauses.test_plan: tools/gen_property_presence_manifest.py must classify every tristate audit target with zero unresolved dispositions; the Rust SDK draft202012_runtime and Circle payload tests pin the sole distinct target and its Missing/Null/Value round-trip.

clauses.requirement: Proposal admission atomically records the original Event, mandatory Ack and pending unit. The unique confirmed Seal atomically commits each unit outcome, successful effects and head; rejected units have no effects and all their members stop being pending. No independent signed rejection or arrival-order terminal race exists. Exact retry preserves the original result; a new deferral cannot follow a terminal outcome.
clauses.test_plan: Run shared ordered-unit and atomic MemoryStore regressions, PostgreSQL rejected multi-member unit commit with injected failure and restart, exact replay and post-terminal deferral rejection. Verify missing dependencies remain pending. Check all proposal consumers resolve the exact Seal unit outcome before reporting business success. The human self-principal Ack-less exception omits only the Ack, never the durable unit/result.

clauses.requirement: Fields inside the event_digest preimage MUST NOT commit to the enclosing Event's own event_id, event_digest or any retype of them, nor to the identity of a not-yet-formed sibling Event in the same atomic unit or ordered submit batch; those two classes have no fixed point, MUST be rejected as event_id_digest_mismatch, and MUST NOT be exempted by any registry. Commitments of that kind MUST instead use the counterpart's payload digest or a structure outside the preimage (proofs, receipts). A one-way forward declaration naming a later Event from a separate submission whose canonical bytes the author already froze is constructible and MUST be allowed only when preimage-identity-exemption-registry.json carries an active row for exactly that field and the field's own description declares the forward commitment.

A server admitting foreign governance MUST independently validate its accepted basis: an event-derived Realm genesis binds the derived create Event and its genesis notary; a PCR genesis binds the verified principal inception and critical root anchor. A foreign service report, proof self-report or error suggestion cannot substitute that validation. Successor acceptance verifies the exact complete antichain and atomically persists accepted state. Ordinary authenticated clients instead consume their own Account Station result without local governance history replay.

A cross-object ak.redaction whose target_ref uses the ak:event: form only trims that Event's fields per preserve[] and MUST NOT change any object's state, including the event-derived object minted from a targeted create Event; an object enters state=redacted only through the object typed-id form of target_ref (Message still goes exclusively through ak.message.redact). The two spellings of one 33-octet token land in two distinct ak.component.object.redaction.v1 cells that are independent and never merge; a reducer MUST NOT canonicalize the ak:event: spelling into the derived object typed id.

Snapshot items contain registered full Cell state with explicit state_model and authenticated eligibility context. Snapshot digest hashes {cell,state_model,state}, independently of the Seal security root. Restore verifies retained original events, coverage and closure evidence; byte-level digest agreement alone is insufficient. Wrong family/model, missing required evidence and context mismatches cannot restore an eligible state.
clauses.test_plan: Review model-specific carrier and replay validation, run snapshot digest KAT, then require SDK restore tests for closure reclassification and missing membership. The digest KAT does not prove a complete authenticated restore.

clauses.requirement: state_digest is the RFC 6962 root over complete registered snapshot Cell states. Each leaf is H(0x00 || JCS({cell:item.id,state_model:item.state_model,state:item.state})); nodes use H(0x01 || left || right), odd tails are promoted, and leaves follow CellRef code-point order across indexed chunks. The empty root hashes empty bytes. These leaves are distinct from Seal security-only leaves; missing state_model, lost causal coverage, double wrapping or absent domain separation must fail the root check.

Causal coverage is keyed by CellRef, exact eligibility_context and EventId. Restoring a Cell requires its verified covered_event_ids and heads, or equivalent authenticated replay at that context. A proof of global event_set_commitment membership establishes original input presence only and cannot grant eligibility or prove per-Cell coverage. Missing necessary evidence remains pending; never infer a negative membership result, discard null heads or truncate retained coverage in a way that revives superseded writes.
clauses.test_plan: Run the existing global membership vector for its limited input-set claim. Separately verify per-Cell coverage, signed target derivation, absent versus explicit null, changed eligibility contexts, closure reclassification and authenticated replay; global inclusion alone must never satisfy the Cell coverage check.

clauses.requirement: Historical deadline faults remain auditable but are not embedded in current frontier health. An incomplete bounded pending sample explicitly carries pending_proposals_complete=false and cannot prove absence of a safety gate; it does not invalidate an independently verified Seal basis.
clauses.test_plan: Exercise 129 and 1000 late accepted obligations, verify current health and complete paginated retained history; exercise 129 pending obligations and validate explicit incompleteness without deletion. Verify target revoke gates independently of the diagnostic sample.

clauses.requirement: Recovery preserves the durable single-writer fence, frozen exact candidate body, unique lineage, original command outcomes and outbox. Competing security commands execute with revision preconditions; rejected commands have no business effects. Timeouts cannot erase a signed position or authorize a parallel lineage. Cross-Realm atomicity requires one governance Station and one serializable store; unsupported cross-Station dependencies fail before any effect.
clauses.test_plan: Inject restart, lease expiry and old-worker revival, stale basis, old Ack authority rotation, bounded backlog and damaged individual records. Check durable outcomes and progress of independently authorized work; missing recovery prerequisites are reported instead of silently clearing gates.

clauses.requirement: Forbidden-wire contexts and matchers are registered and resolved before matching; root fields do not apply to arbitrary descendants or another owning schema. Message.track_name is forbidden while the message-create signed payload retains it.
clauses.test_plan: Run vocabulary mutation gates plus shared SDK and cotest scanner positives and negatives covering Message versus Event payload, real create object wrappers, nested KDF pointers, literal aggregate matchers and patch descendants.

clauses.requirement: Origin/release services verify exact AccountDevice evidence, origin-Station signer closure, signed-time validity and full AccountId/device binding; first enqueue rechecks current authorization and generation. The Account Station selects and retains the history cut; ordinary requester/signing-input/receipt contain no client trust-anchor fields. Clients retain message/HPKE/signature and recipient binding checks, not governance replay. Device evidence cannot authorize Control Events, notary or organization recovery. The capability-bound Account Station supplies exact historical source-key results, deduplicated by evidence ref, and the accepted group suite. Minimal-metadata receivers retain actual encrypted IdentityLink/LeafNode and source-proof checks; public signer authority and winning-lineage range coverage are server responsibilities. Complete byte-bounded pages and ACKs never skip unresolved sequence slots.
clauses.test_plan: Check old request/receipt trust-anchor fields are rejected and server-selected cut is frozen across exact retries. Run server device-history evidence negatives for missing refs, actor/device/Station substitution, altered authorization, revocation and invalid time. Exercise source relay generation changes before enqueue and historical replay after expiry. Run two-account request/manifest/chunk delivery with client cryptographic checks and zero client governance replay. Check missing/duplicate/surplus signer results fail before ACK, same Principal across Account Stations does not collapse per-record authority, and minimal local tree mismatches still fail. Cover registered suite/range byte-length checks, actual source signatures, singleton page admission, byte-prefix cursors, reserved sequence holes and completion after restart. Verify durable record/result installation before ACK without a client checkpoint.

clauses.requirement: Any equivalent Bound endorsement accepted by the Realm confirmed sequence can establish ordinary participant authority; the display representative is not an authority head. Distinct binding semantics, wrong Strand and missing confirmation fail closed. Ordinary admission uses the receiving Station's authenticated Contact intervals and known revocations without requiring origin or governance Station availability. Founding evidence never becomes an ordinary origin co-signature requirement. Clients consume exact Station results without replaying governance history.
clauses.test_plan: Run Direct Conversation authority and capability-ref tests with one, repeated and concurrent equivalent endorsements, missing confirmation, foreign participants and wrong Strand. Execute bidirectional encrypted messages with origin and governance Station offline beyond the old query TTL, known Contact revocation, and reload with real accounts. Client refresh failure must preserve an accepted binding; authenticated blockers and peer/account changes must invalidate it, and delayed responses cannot reinstall old context. Schema fixtures reject found without binding_event_ref.

clauses.requirement: Only the exact founder uses registered provisional message authority before peer durable Welcome, with accepted Genesis and current gates. First accepted Bound permanently exits bootstrap; equivalent later endorsements cannot reactivate it.
clauses.test_plan: Run registered provisional-source policy tests; block exact private Realm claim at epoch 0 and consume after Add, then verify real submitted message epoch, peer since_join boundary and eventual convergence. Test post-Bound rejection of bootstrap authority and equivalent endorsement accumulation.

clauses.requirement: Contact glare requests are exactly two distinct typed EventId wire strings in strict UTF-8 unsigned-byte lexical order, with receipt digests excluded as keys and tiebreakers. Receiving verifiers reject reversed or duplicate refs without normalization before deriving the round ID or founder. Participant ordering separately uses full ActorId RFC 8785 JCS bytes.
clauses.test_plan: Run tools/check_contact_round_kat.py and the SDK Contact round KAT against the same wire-order, digest-order and object-order distinction, reversed input and duplicate refs with equal or different receipt digests. Verify source construction and receiving admission use the same SDK comparison. These checks cover ordering, not a complete two-Station glare flow.

clauses.requirement: A Control Proposal Ack intake request explicitly selects online or delayed publication. Online forbids an AuthorizationLease and re-evaluates current accepted authority; delayed requires an independently valid Event-bound lease. A malformed, invalid or expired delayed request never downgrades to online, and neither branch turns the Ack into a lease or a Seal.
clauses.test_plan: Validate schema and shared SDK positive cases for online without a lease and delayed with a matching lease; reject online with a lease, delayed without one, invalid or expired leases, mode replacement, Event substitution and cross-actor or cross-scope lease reuse. Verify exact retry preserves the first durable Ack and deadline.

clauses.requirement: A v1 Realm or Circle durable ak.mls.proposal is authored only by a Member sender whose leaf is occupied in the exact accepted base and whose leaf credential and signature key equal the verified Event producer executed_by ?? actor_id. ExternalSender, NewMemberProposal, NewMemberCommit, external_init and any app_custom codepoint without an active application registry row fail closed with unsupported_feature and are never reported as schema_violation; standard Member proposal types keep their existing rules.

Result-consuming Stations authenticate exact single-authority governance conclusions without unrelated private replay. Only the configured signer may attest facts. Context, Realm/configuration, query scope and target are bound; absence differs from written null. Execution, current authorization and end-to-end cryptography remain separate.
clauses.test_plan: tools/test_seal_conclusions.py runs schema and real Ed25519 consumer vectors for the sole signer and rejection of signature arrays, wrong configuration/context/target, selector omission, absence/null, interval bounds, bootstrap and resolve carriers. It does not prove production single-writer signing, handoff durability, live revocation or complete join/history execution; those remain in arkret-work 2247/1636/1701.

clauses.requirement: Ordinary clients bootstrap from an independently selected Station origin, fetch public describe without credentials or redirects, and durably compare identity and authentication bindings before authentication or credential reuse. Changes require explicit re-enrollment and fresh authentication; client DID-history replay is not required and independent server verification remains mandatory.
clauses.test_plan: Run SDK models-discovery station_connection cases for selected/preconfigured identity, split authority, issuer replacement, inert changes and invalid routes; run http-client public bootstrap redirect/encoding/size negatives. Run Inkson durable store restart, concurrent installation, corruption and explicit replacement cases, OIDC issuer tests and native/wasm compilation. Audit connection and callback gating, frozen authentication context and credential disposal at explicit re-enrollment. These focused checks do not prove a complete live cross-Station deployment or browser authentication flow.

clauses.requirement: supported_profiles is the sole complete-profile self-declaration. verified_profiles ids are unique and contained in supported_profiles, with independently verified evidence. Both calendar profiles require nonempty executable registered TZDB releases.
clauses.test_plan: Run tools.test_residual_simplification and full schema fixtures for both calendar profiles, supported/verified advertisements, missing/empty/unknown TZDB, forbidden claimed_profiles and verified subset violations. This is schema and reference semantic evidence, not a live profile activation or calendar execution test.

clauses.requirement: Self signer keys omit actor/method mirrors, retain complete selector association and invocation context, preserve mandatory current/Agent authorization_ref, and leave Signal standalone identity and peer portable evidence intact.
clauses.test_plan: Run tools.test_self_signer_result_schema and tools.test_residual_simplification for closed query keys, mandatory authorization, historical separation, reordered/unavailable results, duplicate/missing selectors, different methods/Events and invocation mismatch. Runtime authorization, producer signatures and Signal gates remain required and tracked by the existing owner.

clauses.requirement: Last-resort expiry bounds new distribution only, not historical Welcome decryption with the matching compromised key. Future confidentiality recovery requires effective unknown secret updates and the MLS threat conditions; old plaintext is not made confidential again.
clauses.test_plan: Run tools.test_residual_simplification with keypackage-lifecycle-fixture expiry_security_case for deterministic HPKE GroupSecrets decryption after expiry and failure under an independent fresh key. Synthetic encrypted_group_info context means this is not a full MLS/Station test. The lifecycle vector separately requires product-runner rejection of new expired claims and real group self-updates without retrospective secrecy claims.
